edit.description: The refusal lands in `member_projection_path` **before** the locus dispatch, not inside `splice_name`: the directory-unit branch (1041) never reaches the splice, so guarding the splice alone would leave a slashed name admitted for one shape. Once a path is derived, match it against the deriving kind's own glob through `crate::glob::compile_glob` (the one glob engine) — relative to `governs_root` for an `at` locus, relative to the host's unit for a nested file child — and refuse before a byte is written when it fails: a projection its glob cannot find is written yet ungoverned, counted `(0)` with no finding (invariant 6). Two new `DriftError` variants beside `FlatGlobDepth`/`NestedFileLocus`: `MemberNameSeparator` (the name carries `/` — identity is a file stem or one starred segment, and `/` is the address separator) and `UngovernedProjection` (naming the member, the derived path and the glob that cannot find it).

The SDK half refuses a `/`-carrying member name over `orderedMembers`' projected set (874) — total, like the engine's — reusing `isOneSegment` from `sdk/src/member-address.ts`, the existing home for this predicate (`kind.ts`'s `refuseSegmentedKey` already holds it one grain down), rather than adding a second `/` test inside `spliceName`, which only the link-derivation path reaches. `projectionPath`'s doc comment names the round trip as the property the two derivations share.

The inbox reproduction as a test: a flat `*.json` kind with a member named `a/b/sub/x` refuses naming the separator rather than writing `docs/a/b/sub/x.json` outside its glob; and a derived path that fails its kind's glob refuses rather than emitting.

The lane's harness covers every unit shape; assert each target's emitted `source_path` is matched by its own kind's glob, so agreement and discoverability are both frozen. Its own `guide` fixture (76) carries the same mis-declared `glob: "GUIDE.md"` at `unitShape: "directory"` the two fixture files below do, and takes the same one-token correction to `*/GUIDE.md`.

Fixture correction, no new behavior: the `guide` kind at 244 and 276 declares `unitShape: "directory"` at `glob: "GUIDE.md"`, and a directory unit lands its entry file one segment deep (`<name>/GUIDE.md`) while `import::collect_glob` matches a glob segment-by-segment from the locus root — so that glob reaches only `.claude/guides/GUIDE.md` and the host's own projection is written yet ungoverned, exactly what this entry refuses. `glob: "GUIDE.md"` becomes `glob: "*/GUIDE.md"` on both lines (the declared shape: `src/builtin_kind.rs:123` spells `skill`'s `*/SKILL.md`, `tests/it/gauntlet.rs:67` already spells `*/GUIDE.md`). No assertion in either test moves — the derived path is byte-identical.

The same mis-declared glob at 819. It stays green either way (the SDK half does no glob match, having no matcher), but it is a fixture teaching a shape the engine now refuses: same one-token fix to `*/GUIDE.md`.
The SDK half: a member name carrying `/` refuses at compose time, naming the address separator.

The existing pin needs no edit — its window is the discovery pass, which emit never enters. A new pin over `emit` freezes the round trip at one compile per distinct glob (measured: 2 compiles for 400 members of 2 kinds), per `specs/process/engineering.md`, "Cost scale is hoisted, and pinned by count": the pin is a count, never a clock.

summary: Placement round-trips through discovery: refuse loud when a derived projection path is one its own kind's glob cannot find — a slashed member name among them

tests.asserts: a name carrying `/` and a derived path its glob cannot match both refuse loud, before any byte is written
every emitted member's path is discovered by its own kind's glob
the SDK refuses a `/`-carrying member name with the separator named
the two `guide` fixtures still emit and check byte-identically once their directory-unit glob is spelled `*/GUIDE.md`

acceptance: `cargo test` and `pnpm --dir sdk test` green, with the two new refusals covered and every existing projection still round-tripping (the seam lane's per-target glob assertion passes for every unit shape it covers).
notes: Routed from the inbox: notes 2 and 4 (observed at 040e2d1c / 022477c4); re-scoped from a refactor capture — a first attempt wrote the whole refusal and hit red on the three mis-declared directory-unit fixtures above, two of them outside the old fence. Discovery already descends multi-segment globs (`import::scan_locus`), so the round trip is a real property, not a new capability. Serialized behind the splice-rule entry. scoped at 279b2d15
